args.body:
File: src/util/money.ts

In parseAmount, the regex `/[\s€$£¥]/g` used to strip whitespace and currency symbols does not include ₹ (or other non-listed symbols/letter codes like CHF) so amounts such as '₹1,250.00' or 'CHF 1\'200.00' fail the final digit-only regex test and return null. Broaden the symbol/whitespace stripping (e.g. strip any leading currency symbol or ISO code, and support alternate thousands separators like the Swiss apostrophe) instead of a hard-coded small set of symbols.

file: src/util/money.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.
parseAmount in src/util/money.ts only strips `[\s€$£¥]` before validating with `/^\d+(\.\d+)?$/`; ₹ is not in that character class, so '₹1,250.00' leaves the ₹ in the string and fails the regex, producing the 'amount is not a number' error seen in the issue. The same code would also fail on 'CHF 1'200.00' since CHF letters and the apostrophe separator aren't handled either.
